newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT deal seen boosting its shares.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT deal seen boosting its shares.

text.p: Shares in Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV are set to rise when the Dutch bourse opens at 0730 GMT on Wednesday, boosted by news of its 2.7 billion guilder bid for TNT Ltd.

"The share price will probably go up. People react mostly positively to any kind of takeover. It won't be up by much, probably 20 cents at first," said one analyst. Dutch PTT shares closed at 58.90 guilders on Tuesday.
"People will like this because it will enhance earnings," said another analyst, adding that it might also be seen as positive because Dutch PTT is developing outside of telecoms.

"People might see this as developing the other string to their bow," said the analyst, declining to be named. "If you can manoeuvre yourself away from the telecoms battlefield a little that could be positive because it's a market with a lot of new issues on the horizon," he said.
Other analysts said at first sight the agreed bid for the Australian transport company looked a sound, if somewhat unexciting extension of its own businesses.
"From the risk profile we're not too enthusiastic about it. We don't really think this is the move that's going to put them far apart from everyone else," said ING analyst Eric de Graaf.

"It's going to change the risk profile of the company substantially in our view. It's a more cyclical business, it's much more dependent on world wide economic activity. We think it's even more competitive than the current telecom markets," said De Graaf.
Dutch PTT said it would be financing the offer by providing working capital facilities for the combined group by means of existing cash resources and a 2.25 billion guilder revolving credit facility.
Its A$2.45 per share offer for TNT represents a premium of some 48 percent on TNT's share price before the bid.

Some analysts questioned the sum Dutch PTT was prepared to pay for TNT. "They're not going to get it cheap starting with a premium of 50 percent over the current share price in my view that's not the bottom of the possibilities," said one.
